articles.title: Rustboro keeps the ball, finishes late and closes on Petalburg
articles.dek: Philly Gabite scores twice, Shawn Watzon spreads 263 passing yards among nine receivers, and the Stone answer a 98-yard return in a 32–14 win over Canalave.
articles.author: tessa-wren

body.text: Rustboro spent much of the first half keeping the ball and very little of it adding to the score. The Stone ran an eighty-seven-yard touchdown drive, then a seventy-seven-yard possession that ended on downs. They led Canalave 7–0 at the break. By the finish, their patience had produced five touchdowns, a 32–14 victory and a much more useful place in the division race: one game behind Petalburg, with the Pride coming to Rustboro next.

Philly Gabite carried seventeen times for eighty-four yards and two touchdowns. Shawn Watzon completed twenty-four of thirty-one passes for 263 yards, two scores and no interceptions. The Stone gained 412 yards against Canalave’s 129, earned twenty-two first downs to six and never punted. Those advantages required repeated decisions to continue on fourth down, followed by enough execution to make the decisions worthwhile.

Tyler Scarboro was asked afterward about keeping his offense on the field. “People talk about possession like owning a chair,” the Rustboro coach said. “You can sit in it all afternoon and accomplish nothing. We had that nineteen-play drive and got no points. Nice chair. The other drives, we finished. That is the part I liked.” Rustboro had moved the ball on both first-half possessions but finished only one with points.

Rustboro improved to 9–6 after the previous week’s 41–7 loss at Sunyshore. Canalave fell to 7–8, two games behind Eterna in Sinnoh West. Neither team had secured a playoff berth when the afternoon ended. The Stone can qualify with a win or tie against Petalburg. The Bulwark host Snowpoint next and need to improve their position before a final trip to Oreburgh.
The long possessions that built a narrow lead

Canalave’s opening series reached third-and-one before Slowking was stopped for no gain by Smoke Break, Rustboro’s Gigalith. Vikavolt punted, Joe returned it six yards, and the Stone began an eighty-seven-yard march. Watzon converted third-and-four with five yards to Sudowoodo and another third-and-four with nine to SEARED BITE. The drive became more demanding when a six-yard pass to Nidorina left fourth-and-four.

Watzon answered with a nine-yard completion short left to Nuzleaf, then went deep right to the same receiver for twenty-two. A ten-yard throw to Diggersby preceded Philly Gabite’s two-yard touchdown run to the right with forty-six seconds left in the quarter. Fifteen plays had produced seven points. The Stone had used short completions to remain on the field and a deeper throw to accelerate the final portion of the possession.

“They put the ball there, I finished it,” Gabite said. “People can discuss how many yards looked impressive. Two was the correct number.” His longest run on the day was eleven yards. The value came from repeated useful carries and two finishes near the goal line, rather than one long run that could disguise an otherwise unproductive afternoon.

Rustboro’s next possession lasted nineteen plays and covered seventy-seven yards, yet ended with Watchog losing a yard on fourth-and-one. Medicham made the stop with forty seconds left in the half. Earlier in the drive Watzon had converted fourth-and-one with a three-yard run, and Watchog had gained seven on fourth-and-two. Canalave finally made the fourth-down resistance decisive. The result kept a game of uneven possession within one touchdown.

That sequence gives the halftime score its proper context. Canalave had twice punted, while Rustboro’s only two first-half possessions had consumed substantial ground and time. The Bulwark defense was spending long stretches on the field and still protecting a manageable deficit. Froslass broke up two consecutive throws late in the second drive, and Medicham supplied its ending. Rustboro’s ability to continue drives had been established; its ability to finish every one of them had not.
Manectric answers in one return

The Stone opened the second half with another seventy-five-yard touchdown drive. Passimian sacked Watzon for eight yards, but the quarterback recovered the possession through Gengar: five yards short right, then twenty-eight deep through the middle on third-and-thirteen. The drive finished with a one-yard pass short right to Nidorina on third-and-one. Gorebyss’s kick put Rustboro ahead 14–0.

Manectric returned the ensuing kickoff ninety-eight yards for a touchdown. The game log places the kickoff at 2:22 in the third quarter; Vikavolt’s extra point made it 14–7. Rustboro had required twelve plays to create its touchdown. Canalave’s return unit answered without involving the offense at all. Manectric finished with 180 yards and a touchdown on four returns, the largest individual source of field position and scoring opportunity the Bulwark had.

body.alt: Manectric #14. Manectric returned a third-quarter kickoff ninety-eight yards for Canalave’s first touchdown.
body.caption: Manectric returned a third-quarter kickoff ninety-eight yards for Canalave’s first touchdown.

body.text: “The people in front of me did their work,” Manectric said. “I got the part everybody remembers. I would rather we had given them a win to remember with it.” The return mattered immediately because it prevented Rustboro’s long drives from creating a comfortable advantage. It also left Canalave dependent on finding another kind of scoring possession before the Stone finished again.

Rustboro’s answer began with Gabite running eleven yards right and Watzon finding SEARED BITE for sixteen on a deep throw to that side. Delcatty then sacked Watzon for four yards, helping force another fourth down. Gabite converted fourth-and-two with five yards left. The Stone kept going into the final quarter and faced fourth-and-one again, this time with a considerably larger gain available.

Watzon threw deep left to Gibby Timmy for twenty-three yards. On the next play Gabite scored from two yards out, this time through the middle, with 5:02 remaining. Cetitan blocked the extra point, leaving Rustboro ahead 20–7. The Stone had answered the return with another seventy-five-yard touchdown possession and two more fourth-down conversions. Their approach demanded execution; that drive supplied it in two different forms.
The six-point game that lasted one possession

Canalave finally produced its own sustained scoring response. Slowking found Grafaiai deep right for thirty-one yards, then completed throws to Manectric for ten, Seviper for twelve and Torterra for sixteen. Delcatty scored on a one-yard run through the middle at 3:59. Vikavolt converted, and the Bulwark were within 20–14 despite the large differences in total yards and first downs.

Four of Slowking’s five completions came on that drive. He finished five-for-thirteen for ninety-four yards, with neither a touchdown pass nor an interception. The six-play scoring possession showed what Canalave could do when it completed throws beyond the initial line of defense. The rest of the afternoon gave the Bulwark too few such sequences: they converted one of five third downs and rushed for thirty-five yards on twelve attempts.

Gengar returned the next squib kick thirty yards, and Watzon immediately found Gibby Timmy deep right for forty-one. Gabite followed with runs of seven and six. After Watzon lost two yards, Watchog scored through the middle from nine yards out at the two-minute mark. The two-point attempt failed when Kecleon broke up the pass to SEARED BITE. Rustboro led 26–14, having answered Canalave’s only offensive touchdown with another of its own.

body.alt: Archeops #99, Porygon-Z #37. Gibby Timmy’s forty-one-yard reception helped Rustboro extend its fourth-quarter lead.
body.caption: Gibby Timmy’s forty-one-yard reception helped Rustboro extend its fourth-quarter lead.

body.text: “I just tried to get through what was there,” Watchog said. “The line and the passes had done so much before that. I did not want to waste it.” He finished with forty-seven yards and the touchdown on twelve carries. Together with Gabite, he supplied 131 yards on twenty-nine carries. Rustboro finished with thirty-five team rushing attempts and 149 yards, enough production to support its short passing game.

The Bulwark’s next four passes fell incomplete. Joe and Frosmoth each broke one up, and Rustboro took over on downs. Gabite supplied three carries before Watzon found Sudowoodo short right for a ten-yard touchdown on third-and-four with 1:30 left. Gorebyss missed the extra point wide left. Three fourth-quarter touchdowns had supplied eighteen points, taking the game from 14–7 at the quarter break to its final 32–14 score.
A useful win before two division opponents

Watzon spread his twenty-four completions among nine receivers. Gibby Timmy led with sixty-four yards on two catches; SEARED BITE caught five for fifty-three, Gengar four for fifty and Nuzleaf three for forty-one. The late explosive throws mattered, but the distribution explains how Rustboro kept finding another answer when an earlier attempt failed. “Stay with the next play,” Watzon said. “There was usually something there.”

The Stone also received substantial recorded work up front: Aggron had nine pancakes and Crustle seven, each with a ninety-seven percent block-win figure. Canalave registered two sacks and broke up passes, but could not consistently finish possessions with the ball changing hands. Rustboro converted eight of thirteen third downs and repeatedly survived the fourth downs that followed the others.

Milotic’s new six-week injury designation complicates the next assignment for the Stone; the record does not identify an exact injury time. Petalburg arrives with a chance to clinch Hoenn West by winning, while Rustboro can secure a berth by avoiding defeat and keep a stronger division challenge alive by winning. Dewford follows in Week 18. Rustboro has two home games left, both against teams directly involved in deciding its postseason position.
